subject: Physics
title: Sample Practice Paper 1: Mechanics and Electricity (unofficial, not a genuine AQA past paper)
paperText:
1. A car of mass 1200 kg accelerates uniformly from rest to 18 m/s in 6.0 seconds.
(a) Calculate the acceleration of the car. [2 marks]
(b) Calculate the resultant force needed to produce this acceleration. [2 marks]

2. A ball is dropped from rest from a height of 20 m above the ground. Air resistance is negligible.
(a) Calculate the speed of the ball just before it hits the ground. [3 marks]
(b) Calculate the time taken for the ball to fall. [2 marks]

3. State what is meant by terminal velocity, and explain, in terms of the forces acting, why a skydiver falling through air reaches it. [4 marks]

4. A component has a potential difference of 12 V across it and a current of 0.5 A flowing through it.
(a) Calculate the resistance of the component. [2 marks]
(b) Calculate the power dissipated by the component. [2 marks]

5. A wave has a frequency of 50 Hz and a wavelength of 6.0 m. Calculate the speed of the wave. [2 marks]

6. Sketch a graph of velocity against time for the ball in Question 2, from the moment it is released to the moment just before it lands, labelling the axes with appropriate values. [3 marks]
markSchemeText:
1(a). a = (v-u)/t = (18-0)/6.0. M1 for correct substitution into a suvat equation. A1 for a = 3.0 m/s^2. [2 marks total]
1(b). F = ma = 1200 x 3.0. M1 for correct use of F=ma with their value of a. A1 for F = 3600 N. [2 marks total]

2(a). v^2 = u^2 + 2as, with u=0, a=9.81, s=20. M1 for correct substitution. A1 for v = 19.8 (or 19.81) m/s, accept 20 m/s to 2 s.f. [3 marks total, allow ecf from incorrect but consistent working]
2(b). Using v = u + at with their v from 2(a). M1 for correct rearrangement/substitution. A1 for t = 2.0 s (accept answers consistent with their 2(a)). [2 marks total]

3. B1 for stating terminal velocity is the maximum/constant speed reached by a falling object. B1 for stating it occurs when air resistance (drag) equals weight. B1 for explaining that the resultant force is then zero. B1 for explaining that with zero resultant force, acceleration is zero, so speed stays constant. [4 marks total]

4(a). R = V/I = 12/0.5. M1 for correct use of Ohm's law. A1 for R = 24 ohms. [2 marks total]
4(b). P = IV = 0.5 x 12. M1 for correct use of P=IV (or equivalent form). A1 for P = 6.0 W. [2 marks total]

5. v = f x lambda = 50 x 6.0. M1 for correct substitution into wave speed equation. A1 for v = 300 m/s. [2 marks total]

6. B1 for a straight line through the origin with positive gradient (constant acceleration, no terminal velocity reached as air resistance is negligible). B1 for correctly labelled axes (velocity in m/s on y-axis, time in s on x-axis). B1 for the line ending at approximately (2.0, 20) consistent with answers to Question 2. [3 marks total]
